# SAP 如何利用 AI 现代化 HMRC 的税务基础设施
2026年2月2日
![SAP 总部，HMRC 选择该公司来改造其核心收入系统，并将 AI 置于英国税务管理策略的核心。](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/sap-ai-hmrc-finance-tax-infrastructure-data-sovereignty-governance-public-sector-automation-artificial-intelligence-1024x768.jpg)
HMRC 已选择 [SAP](https://www.sap.com/index.html) 来改造其核心收入系统，并将 AI 置于英国税务管理策略的核心。
该合同代表了公共部门机构如何处理自动化的一个更广泛的变化。与其在遗留基础设施上叠加 AI 工具，HMRC 正在替换底层架构，以支持机器学习和自动决策。
AI 驱动的现代化工作重点是企业税务管理平台（ETMP），这是负责管理每年超过8000亿英镑税收的技术骨干，目前支持超过45个税制。通过 RISE with SAP 将此基础设施迁移到托管云环境中，HMRC 旨在简化数万名员工每天依赖的复杂技术环境。
有效的机器学习需要[统一的数据集](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/franny-hsiao-salesforce-scaling-enterprise-ai/)，这在碎片化的本地遗留系统中往往难以维护。作为部署的一部分，HMRC 将实施 SAP 业务技术平台和 AI 功能。这些工具旨在更快地提供洞察并自动化税务管理中的流程。
### SAP 主权云满足本地 AI 采用要求
在高度监管的领域部署 AI 需要严格的数据治理。HMRC 将在 SAP 的英国主权云上托管这些新功能。这确保了税务机关在采用商业 AI 工具时，遵守关于数据驻留、安全性和合规性的本地要求。
“像 HMRC 提供的大规模公共系统必须在全国范围内可靠运行，同时适应不断变化的需求，”SAP 英国及爱尔兰地区总经理 Leila Romane 表示。
“通过现代化英国最重要的平台之一，并将其托管在英国主权云上，我们正在帮助加强关键国家基础设施的韧性、安全性和可持续性。”
### 使用 AI 现代化税务基础设施
最终，现代化的目标是减少纳税人的互动摩擦。SAP 和 HMRC 将合作定义新的 AI 功能，专门用于改善纳税人体验和增强决策。
对于企业领导者来说，这里的教训是数据可访问性和运营价值之间的联系。这种合作为 HMRC 员工提供了更好的分析数据访问和改进的用户界面。这种结构支持对实时分析和报告的信心；允许为纳税人提供更响应和透明的体验。

# [How SAP is modernising HMRC’s tax infrastructure with AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/how-sap-modernising-hmrc-tax-infrastructure-with-ai/)
February 2, 2026
![SAP headquarters as HMRC selects the company to overhaul its core revenue systems and place AI at the centre of the UK’s tax administration strategy.](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/sap-ai-hmrc-finance-tax-infrastructure-data-sovereignty-governance-public-sector-automation-artificial-intelligence-1024x768.jpg)

## [AI Business Strategy](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/ai-business-strategy/)  [AI in Action](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/)  [Finance AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/finance-ai/)  [Governance, Regulation & Policy](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/new_governance-regulation-and-policy/)  [Government & Public Sector AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-in-action/government-public-sector-ai/)  [Inside AI](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/inside-ai/)
HMRC has selected [SAP](https://www.sap.com/index.html) to overhaul its core revenue systems and place AI at the centre of the UK’s tax administration strategy.
The contract represents a broader shift in how public sector bodies approach automation. Rather than layering AI tools over legacy infrastructure, HMRC is replacing the underlying architecture to support machine learning and automated decision-making natively.
The AI-powered modernisation effort focuses on the Enterprise Tax Management Platform (ETMP), the technological backbone responsible for managing over £800 billion in annual tax revenue and which currently supports over 45 tax regimes. By migrating this infrastructure to a managed cloud environment via RISE with SAP, HMRC aims to simplify a complex technology landscape that tens of thousands of staff rely on daily.
Effective machine learning requires [unified data sets](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/franny-hsiao-salesforce-scaling-enterprise-ai/), which are often impossible to maintain across fragmented on-premise legacy systems. As part of the deployment, HMRC will implement SAP Business Technology Platform and AI capabilities. These tools are designed to surface insights faster and automate processes across tax administration.
### SAP Sovereign Cloud meets local AI adoption requirements
Deploying AI in such highly-regulated sectors requires strict data governance. HMRC will host these new capabilities on SAP’s UK Sovereign Cloud. This ensures that while the tax authority adopts commercial AI tools, it adheres to localised requirements regarding data residency, security, and compliance.
“Large-scale public systems like those delivered by HMRC must operate reliably at national scale while adapting to changing demands,” said Leila Romane, Managing Director UKI at SAP.
“By modernising one of the UK’s most important platforms and hosting it on a UK sovereign cloud, we are helping to strengthen the resilience, security, and sustainability of critical national infrastructure.”
### Using AI to modernise tax infrastructure
The modernisation ultimately aims to reduce friction in taxpayer interactions. SAP and HMRC will work together to define new AI capabilities specifically aimed at improving taxpayer experiences and enhancing decision-making.
For enterprise leaders, the lesson here is the link between data accessibility and operational value. The collaboration provides HMRC employees with better access to analytical data and an improved user interface. This structure supports greater confidence in real-time analysis and reporting; allowing for more responsive and transparent experiences for taxpayers.

*#* *T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*：*关*于*新*一*代*代*理*交*付*现*代*分*析*
*2*0*2*6*年*2*月*2*日*
*!*[*]*(*h*t*t*p*s*:*/*/*w*w*w*.*a*r*t*i*f*i*c*i*a*l*i*n*t*e*l*l*i*g*e*n*c*e*-*n*e*w*s*.*c*o*m*/*w*p*-*c*o*n*t*e*n*t*/*u*p*l*o*a*d*s*/*2*0*2*6*/*0*2*/*s*t*e*v*e*-*j*o*h*n*s*o*n*-*_*0*i*V*9*L*m*P*D*n*0*-*u*n*s*p*l*a*s*h*-*1*0*2*4*x*5*7*6*.*j*p*g*)*
*如*果*你*是*数*据*和*分*析*领*域*的*领*导*者*，*那*么*你*一*定*知*道*代*理*型*A*I*正*在*以*前*所*未*有*的*速*度*推*动*变*革*。*知*道*你*需*要*做*些*什*么*和*知*道*具*体*该*怎*么*做*是*两*回*事*。*好*消*息*是*像*T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*这*样*的*提*供*商*能*够*提*供*帮*助*，*该*公*司*用*他*们*自*己*的*话*说*，*决*心*从*头*开*始*重*新*构*想*分*析*和*B*I*。*
*“*当*然*，*代*理*系*统*确*实*将*我*们*带*入*了*全*新*的*领*域*，*”*T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*的*首*席*数*据*和*A*I*官*J*a*n*e* *S*m*i*t*h*解*释*说*。*“*它*们*使*我*们*从*被*动*报*告*转*向*更*主*动*的*决*策*制*定*。*
*“*传*统*的*B*I*等*待*你*发*现*见*解*，*”*J*a*n*e*补*充*道*。*“*而*代*理*系*统*则*全*天*候*地*从*多*个*来*源*监*控*数*据*；*它*们*诊*断*变*化*的*原*因*；*并*自*动*触*发*下*一*步*行*动*。*
*“*我*们*变*得*更*加*注*重*行*动*。*”*
*除*了*从*被*动*到*主*动*的*变*化*之*外*，*J*a*n*e*还*看*到*了*B*I*在*两*个*其*他*方*面*的*变*化*。*一*方*面*，*向*“*真*正*的*数*据*民*主*化*”*转*变*，*另*一*方*面*则*是*对*“*语*义*层*”*的*重*新*关*注*。*“*当*代*理*不*严*格*理*解*业*务*背*景*时*，*它*无*法*以*我*刚*才*描*述*的*方*式*采*取*行*动*，*”*J*a*n*e*说*。*“*强*大*的*语*义*层*是*真*正*理*解*A*I*混*乱*的*唯*一*方*法*。*”*
*T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*有*一*系*列*代*理*来*采*取*行*动*并*为*客*户*带*来*改*变*。*去*年*1*2*月*，*公*司*推*出*了*四*个*新*的*B*I*代*理*，*这*些*代*理*作*为*一*个*团*队*工*作*，*以*提*供*现*代*分*析*。*
*S*p*o*t*t*e*r* *3*是*首*次*亮*相*于*2*0*2*4*年*底*的*一*个*代*理*的*最*新*迭*代*版*本*，*它*是*明*星*产*品*。*它*可*以*与*S*l*a*c*k*和*S*a*l*e*s*f*o*r*c*e*等*应*用*程*序*进*行*对*话*，*不*仅*可*以*回*答*问*题*，*还*可*以*评*估*其*答*案*的*质*量*，*并*不*断*尝*试*直*到*得*到*正*确*的*结*果*。*
*“*它*利*用*了**[*模*型*上*下*文**]*协*议*，*因*此*你*可*以*向*组*织*的*结*构*化*数*据*—*—*你*的*所*有*行*、*列*、*表*—*—*提*问*，*同*时*也*可*以*结*合*非*结*构*化*数*据*，*”*J*a*n*e*说*。*“*这*样*，*你*可*以*通*过*我*们*的*代*理*或*你*自*己*的*大*语*言*模*型*获*得*非*常*丰*富*的*上*下*文*答*案*。*”*
*然*而*，*这*种*力*量*也*带*来*了*责*任*。*正*如*T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*最*近*的*一*本*电*子*书*[*探*讨*2*0*2*6*年*的*数*据*和*A*I*趋*势*]*(*h*t*t*p*s*:*/*/*g*o*.*t*h*o*u*g*h*t*s*p*o*t*.*c*o*m*/*e*b*o*o*k*-*a*i*-*d*a*t*a*-*t*r*e*n*d*s*-*2*0*2*6*.*h*t*m*l*)*所*指*出*的*那*样*，*C*级*高*管*需*要*设*计*系*统*，*以*便*每*个*决*策*—*—*无*论*是*人*类*还*是*A*I*做*出*的*—*—*都*可*以*被*解*释*、*改*进*和*信*任*。*
*T*h*o*u*g*h*t*S*p*o*t*将*这*种*新*兴*架*构*称*为*“*决*策*智*能*”*（*D*I*）*。*“*我*认*为*我*们*会*看*到*很*多*的*是*决*策*供*应*链*，*”*J*a*n*e*解*释*说*。*“*与*其*说*是*单*一*的*见*解*，*我*认*为*我*们*将*看*到*的*是*决*策*…*…*通*过*可*重*复*的*阶*段*流*动*，*数*据*分*析*、*模*拟*、*行*动*、*反*馈*，*这*些*都*是*人*机*之*间*的*互*动*，*可*以*记*录*在*一*个*我*们*可*以*称*之*为*决*策*系*统*记*录*的*东*西*中*。*”*
*这*在*实*践*中*会*是*什*么*样*子*？*J*a*n*e*举*了*一*个*制*药*行*业*临*床*试*验*的*例*子*。*“*系*统*会*记*录*并*版*本*化*患*者*如*何*被*选*为*临*床*试*验*对*象*；*如*何*使*用*健*康*记*录*中*的*数*据*来*识*别*候*选*人*；*如*何*根*据*试*验*方*案*模*拟*该*决*定*；*如*何*匹*配*；*以*及*最*终*医*生*如*何*推*荐*该*患*者*参*加*试*验*，*”*她*说*。*
*“*这*些*过*程*可*以*被*审*计*，*可*以*在*下*一*次*试*验*中*改*进*。*但*对*这*一*决*策*流*程*中*的*每*一*个*元*素*进*行*细*致*的*记*录*，*将*其*视*为*一*个*供*应*链*，*是*我*想*象*中*的*方*式*。*”*

# [ThoughtSpot: On the new fleet of agents delivering modern analytics](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/thoughtspot-on-the-new-fleet-of-agents-delivering-modern-analytics/)
February 2, 2026
![](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/steve-johnson-_0iV9LmPDn0-unsplash-1024x576.jpg)
Share this story:
Categories:
## [Artificial Intelligence](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/artificial-intelligence/)  [Human-AI Relationships](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/ai-and-us/human-ai-relationships/)  [TechEx Events](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/techex-events/)
If you are a data and analytics leader, then you know agentic AI is fuelling unprecedented speed of change right now. Knowing you need to do something and knowing what to do, however, are two different things. The good news is providers like ThoughtSpot are able to assist, with the company in its own words determined to [‘reimagin\[e\] analytics and BI from the ground up’](https://www.thoughtspot.com/blog/insights-to-actions-with-agentic-analytics).
“Certainly, agentic systems really are shifting us into very new territory,” explains Jane Smith, field chief data and AI officer at ThoughtSpot. “They’re shifting us away from passive reporting to much more active decision making.
“Traditional BI waits for you to find an insight,” adds Jane. “Agentic systems are proactively monitoring data from multiple sources 24/7; they’re diagnosing why changes happened; they’re triggering the next action automatically.
“We’re getting much more action-oriented.”
Alongside moving from passive to active, there are two other ways in which Jane sees this change taking place in BI. There is a shift towards the ‘true democratisation of data’ on one hand, but on the other is the ‘resurgence of focus’ on the semantic layer. “You cannot have an agent taking action in the way I just described when it doesn’t strictly understand business context,” says Jane. “A strong semantic layer is really the only way to make sense… of the chaos of AI.”
ThoughtSpot has a fleet of agents to take action and move the needle for customers. In December, the company [launched four new BI agents](https://www.thoughtspot.com/press-releases/thoughtspot-launches-four-bi-agents-that-work-as-a-team-to-deliver-modern-analytics), with the idea that they work as a team to deliver modern analytics.
Spotter 3, the latest iteration of an agent first debuted [towards the end of 2024](https://www.thoughtspot.com/blog/introducing-spotter-ai-analyst), is the star. It is conversant with applications like Slack and Salesforce, and can not only answer questions, but assess the quality of its answer and keep trying until it gets the right result.
“It leverages the \[Model Context\] protocol, so you can ask your questions to your organisation’s structured data – everything in your rows, your columns, your tables – but also incorporate your unstructured data,” says Jane. “So, you can get really context-rich answers to questions, all through our agent, or if you wish, through your own LLM.”
With this power, however, comes responsibility. As ThoughtSpot’s recent eBook [exploring data and AI trends for 2026 notes](https://go.thoughtspot.com/ebook-ai-data-trends-2026.html), the C-suite needs to work out how to design systems so every decision – be it human or AI – can be explained, improved, and trusted.
ThoughtSpot calls this emerging architecture ‘decision intelligence’ (DI). “What we’ll see a lot of, I think, will be decision supply chains,” explains Jane. “Instead of a one-off insight, I think what we’re going to see is decisions… flow through repeatable stages, data analysis, simulation, action, feedback, and these are all interactions between humans and machines that will be logged in what we can think of as a decision system of record.”
What would this look like in practice? Jane offers an example from a clinical trial in the pharma industry. “The system would log and version, really, every step of how a patient is chosen for a clinical trial; how data from a health record is used to identify a candidate; how that decision was simulated against the trial protocol; how the matching occurred; how potentially a doctor ultimately recommended this patient for the trial,” she says.
“These are processes that can be audited, they can be improved for the following trial. But the very meticulous logging of every element of the flow of this decision into what we think of as a supply chain is a way that I would visualise that.”
